design_rationale.SL01: Dual panel comparison to juxtapose Japan's foundational excellence against declining metrics - creates visual tension that mirrors the slide's argument
design_rationale.SL02: Horizontal bar chart comparison showing funding growth across nations - Japan's small bar creates immediate visual impact against competitors
design_rationale.SL03: Big number pair with Venn diagram - emphasizes scale of opportunity while showing convergence of theory and practice
design_rationale.SL04: 2x2 domain matrix - organizes four research domains with open problems and stakes, establishing academic legitimacy
design_rationale.SL05: Annotated timeline table - shows publication record in top venues with institutional credibility ribbon
design_rationale.SL06: Program overview card - presents grant information in digestible, action-oriented format with clear deadline
design_rationale.SL07: Problem-solution matching diagram - directly maps PSE problems to required expertise, showing alignment with audience capabilities
design_rationale.SL08: Bridge diagram - visualizes Nyx Foundation's connector role between Japanese academia and Ethereum ecosystem
design_rationale.SL09: Radial stakeholder benefit diagram - shows mutual value flowing to PIs, students, and Ethereum ecosystem
design_rationale.SL10: Horizontal action pathway - three clear steps from review to connection to engagement, with events sidebar

design_principles_applied: Gene Zelazny's chart selection framework: matching visual type to message purpose (comparison, trend, relationship, process)
Edward Tufte's data-ink ratio: maximizing meaningful content, minimizing decorative elements
Avoided default bar charts where other formats better serve the message
Each visual includes explicit takeaway annotation stating the conclusion
Visual specifications detailed enough to be built without additional clarification
